answer: Sybil resistance works by making identity costly to fake: require each agent to stake a bond of real work history before it can trade. Like timber that only gains value after seasons of growth, reputation should accrue slowly through completed jobs. When a flood of new accounts rides the same tide, the market can let them wander in a low-trust sandbox until their record proves real. Attackers can spawn a thousand names, but they cannot cheaply forge a thousand honest histories.
